substeps.caption: An empty bay in a warehouse, about 24 m between the racks on its side walls. Everything that follows goes into it.

The layout goes down in tape first: the 3.0 m aisle, each machine's footprint, and a MiR250 dock at every front with an AprilTag target on a post. Every dock has room at its open end for a MiR to turn on the spot; nothing stands in a dock or on the way into one.

Utilities, in a high bay with a 36 ft roof for the 30 ft Shuttles: cable trays over both rows, round the Shuttles' backs. A drop comes down to every station and ends in a grey junction box with sockets, a network port and an AirGradient air monitor. 208 V three-phase goes to each VLM (#53), argon from a cylinder manifold to the glovebox, the rePowder, the Aconity and the DED, and a duct up from the fume hood. Between the Shuttles, at the back: an N2 generator, a compressor and a chiller for the trays' couplings. Layout choices, not a design.
Two Kardex Shuttle XP 500s, 9.15 m (30 ft) tall, go together where their footprints are taped, 800 mm apart: base frames, posts, storage columns.
The extractors and their drives, then 18 empty trays, A to S: 12 electrified, each with its dock plate at the back right, and 6 plain ones for storage (J, S, N, O, P and Q).
The cladding, the openings (996 mm tall), the consoles and the shutters.

The floor machines, rigged in on pallet jacks and machine skates (the Aconity MIDI is 1450 kg, the 100 kN Instron 799 kg), are set down fronts to the aisle: the glovebox (its antechamber to the aisle), the rePowder, the sieving cell, the Aconity MIDI, the packaging station; across the aisle the two Instrons, the ducted fume hood, the DED and the wire EDM.

For scaling up, beyond the south row's ends, an EOS M 400-4 (large-format LPBF) and a Meltio robot cell (DED repair), fronts to the north, each with a clear strip to the aisle. No MiR250 serves them: their powder, wire and parts come by forklift (notes/scaleup.md).
Two MiR Charge 48V chargers go in, then the first MiR250 rolls onto its charging plate.

Its cabinet goes on top: it carries the arm and holds the UR control box.
The UR control box (460 x 449 x 254 mm, 12 kg) goes into the cabinet.
The UR10e (33.3 kg: two people, or a small hoist) is set on the cabinet's top plate and bolted down: four M8 bolts at 20 Nm, two 8 mm pins so it goes back in the same place (UR's manual).
The Robotiq 2F-85 goes on the flange.
It wakes up and stretches. The second unit is built the same way at the other charger.

Loading, drawn see-through. Most of what goes on a tray weighs 20-110 kg (the S2 PUMA 108 kg, each UPS 8-22), more than the arm's 12.5 kg or one person should lift (NIOSH: 23 kg), so a scissor lift table stands at the opening, its deck level with the tray, and people slide each machine across. The bay cameras go on, two in each bay: Shuttle 2's first, seen by an operator at the opening looking up (the cladding drawn solid for them). They hang from the bay's roof, one at the back looking forward over the presented tray, one behind the header looking back at it.
Then Shuttle 1's: the same two. With the D405 on the arm's wrist, they see what is on every tray the Shuttle presents.

Every tray with instruments carries its own stream cameras; the storage trays (J, N, O, P, Q and S) carry none: the bay camera takes their stock whenever one is presented, the only time a jar or a sample can come or go.
